Hi Sofia — appreciate the clear summary. Attached are two artifacts: a one‑pager (Redwood_Pack_Options_Sept2026.pdf) that compares the two paths and an editable calculator (Plan-Comparison-Calc-20260928.xlsx) that shows month-by-month cash impact for a 3‑month pilot. Key points up front: 

- Feature-bundle (tight SMB-tier + throughput add-on): lowest up-front cost, clear feature entitlement boundaries, fast rollback (switch off add-on). Good if product wants predictable feature access and cost control.
- Partial-swap canary (25% traffic on higher-tier SKU): safer operationally for procurement because it limits exposure and preserves historical usage accounting; slightly higher unit cost during the canary window and requires routing rules + traffic steering.

Recommendation: run a hybrid pilot — start with the partial-swap canary for initial 2 weeks to validate latency/quality under production traffic, then flip to the bundled plan with a temporary throughput add-on if product signals sustained usage. This minimizes procurement risk and keeps product’s UX intact.

Regarding discounts: we can structure a 3‑month phased discount: 30% month 1 (canary), 20% month 2 (ramp), 10% month 3 (post-pilot). If procurement needs deferred credits instead, we can convert to an invoice credit schedule. 

If that sounds OK, I’ll draft the mutual action plan and send a clean commercial note for procurement. 

— Kimberly Park
